If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test expects:
  - It sets a description on OptionBuilder, then intentionally tries to create an option with an invalid short option character ('"'). This should throw IllegalArgumentException and, crucially, must reset OptionBuilder’s static state so that a subsequent create('x') does not inherit the previous description. The assertion checks that the next created option has a null description.

- How OptionBuilder is implemented:
  - withDescription("JUnit") stores the description in a static field (OptionBuilder.description).
  - create(char) delegates to create(String).
  - create(String) constructs a new Option using the current static fields, then sets more properties, and only then calls OptionBuilder.reset() at the end of the method.

- Where the exception occurs:
  - In create(String), the first step is new Option(opt, description).
  - Option’s constructor calls OptionValidator.validateOption(opt). For the single-character opt '"', validation fails and throws IllegalArgumentException.

- Why the state is not reset:
  - Because the IllegalArgumentException is thrown during new Option(opt, description), the rest of create(String) is skipped, including the call to OptionBuilder.reset() at the end. There is no try/finally to ensure reset happens on failure.

- Consequence leading to the failure:
  - After the failed create('"'), the static description remains "JUnit".
  - The next call OptionBuilder.create('x') uses the lingering description and produces an Option whose description is "JUnit".
  - The test’s assertNull on the description therefore fails.

- Summary of the root cause:
  - OptionBuilder.reset() is only invoked on the successful path of create(String). When an IllegalArgumentException is thrown during option construction/validation, the builder’s static state is not reset, causing subsequent options to inherit unwanted settings. The fix is to ensure reset() is called in a finally block (or otherwise guaranteed) within create(String) (and transitively for create(char)).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
